name: Scene
first: A part of an app's user interface whose life cycle the system manages, such as a window, which holds the views it shows.

dependsOn.why: A scene holds the views that it shows.

what.is: A scene is a part of an app's user interface whose life cycle the system manages, such as a window. It holds a view, and the system decides when to show it, how many there are, and when they go to the background.
what.afterExample: `WindowGroup` is the scene that SwiftUI provides for an app's windows. It holds a `Text`, and line 6 prints its type, {{WindowGroup<Text>}}.
what.problem: An app's views need somewhere to be shown, and the system decides where: in one window on an iPhone, in several windows on an iPad or a Mac. A scene tells the system which views go in each window, and the system makes and removes the windows.
what.how: The views given to a `WindowGroup` are the template for each window that the app makes from it. Apple's documentation says that each window keeps its own state: the system makes new storage for the state of the views in each window.

when.text: Use a window group for an app's main windows. On an iPad or a Mac, a person can open more than one window from the same group.
Don't make a scene to show a view inside a screen. A scene is a whole window, or a part of the system's interface such as a settings window. Inside it, the parts of the screen are views.
